explanation: Banjo — a bright, twangy plucked chordophone with a taut membrane head giving a metallic-edged attack and fast decay.
Bluegrass and folk banjo rolls and single notes.
Mandolin — a high, bright double-course plucked chordophone, often played with a shimmering tremolo.
Paired-string courses give a chorused, ringing tone.
Ukulele — a small, bright nylon-strung plucked chordophone with a soft, warm-yet-bright attack and quick decay.
Soprano through baritone ukulele plucks and strums.
Sitar — a buzzy, resonant plucked chordophone whose curved bridge and sympathetic strings create an inharmonic, shimmering drone.
Indian classical melodic lines with characteristic pitch-bending and jawari buzz.
A plucked chordophone that does not fit a specific subcategory, or the abstention target when the scorer is unsure.
